source.title: Spiking Network Initialisation and Firing Rate Collapse
source.authors: Nicolas Perez-Nieves; Dan F. M. Goodman

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including supplementary materials and references.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports simulations of firing rates and gradient propagation in spiking networks under initialization and timestep interventions. These results bear on initialization-related training claims, but it does not test classification training on CIFAR benchmarks.
record.gate_note: The paper tests firing-rate collapse and its proposed corrections in LIF simulations, then tests initialization and gradient behavior in simulated SNNs. It does not report classification training results on real datasets. Results cited from other work are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study adapts ANN variance-propagation initialization methods to SNNs and evaluates firing rates and surrogate-gradient variance at initialization. It reports no learning-speed or trainable-depth outcomes, so these measures do not test V4. Its own results do not test the other versions either.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors propose corrections for discrete-time firing-rate collapse and an SNN initialization strategy combining firing-rate calculations with surrogate-gradient scaling. Their simulations approximately preserve activity and gradient variance under restricted assumptions; effectiveness during training and on real datasets remains unestablished.
record.recipe_differences: The study develops and evaluates initialization and firing-rate correction methods for spiking neural networks; it does not apply the ANN classification-training recipes in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Simulation timestep; spike placement within each timestep; correction method; input rate and number of inputs; target firing rate; surrogate-gradient width Bth.

fits_no_version.finding: LIF simulations lose firing rate as the timestep increases. Random-walk, Wiener-process and permutation corrections recover missing spikes under their respective assumptions, with failures beyond 20ms in these setups.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Discrete-time spike integration can suppress firing rates, and accounting for within-step spike ordering can improve simulation accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: The proposed initialization and firing-rate correction approximately maintain target activity across 20 untrained SNN layers; lower target rates produce an upward bias.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Firing-rate-based initialization can approximately preserve activity across layers in homogeneous Poisson-input SNN simulations.

fits_no_version.finding: Scaling a narrow surrogate derivative substantially reduces gradient-variance decay across 20 layers, although residual decay remains; a wider surrogate gives much worse propagation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Surrogate-derivative scaling can improve gradient-variance propagation at SNN initialization, conditional on surrogate width and temporal-correlation assumptions.

record.problems: Experiments use homogeneous Poisson inputs and simulated LIF populations rather than real datasets. The authors explicitly say applicability to real data and training remains an open question. Several figure results provide means and standard errors but not exact values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible results omitted. Cited results from prior work and theoretical expressions without a reported outcome in this study were not extracted as rows.

untested.parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including random labels and dependence on model size or training recipe.
Spurious local minima and the effect of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student training.
Depth-dependent training degradation, identity shortcuts, and training of deep plain or unnormalized residual networks.
Initialization effects on actual learning speed and trainable depth; orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization and very deep plain convolutional training.
Loss recovery, curvature, sharpness thresholds, and divergence under large learning rates.
Batch normalization effects on accuracy gain, learning-rate tolerance, and comparison with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The record's V4 tested_not_extracted designation should be changed to not tested. Supplementary Figures S3 and S4 add related activity and gradient-propagation results, but neither supplies a missing result on a claim version.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 classification error, random or corrupted labels, model size, and training duration.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student optimization and spurious local minima.
Plain versus residual network depth, batch normalization, ImageNet/CIFAR-10 training error, and Fixup.

The paper reports weight initialization results for SNNs, but its experiments measure firing rates and gradient variance rather than the version’s stated plain ANN training speed/depth outcomes. Theoretical initialization results and related ANN citations do not provide results for that claim.
Training with learning rates above the stability limit and sharpness behavior.
Batch normalization effects on training speed or tolerated learning rates.

rows.operation_detail: Increased simulation timestep and measured output firing rate with spikes placed at the end of each interval (brian2 default).
rows.value: Simulation firing rate tends to zero as ∆t increases
rows.uncertainty: Standard error in the mean across 10 simulations
rows.note: This is a spiking simulation rate result, not a classification-training error result.
rows.check: Firing-rate collapse in an untrained LIF population does not measure any claim version; the recorded absent state must not imply absent optimization effects.

rows.subject: Feed-forward SNN with 20 layers
rows.stage_stated: initialization simulation; not trained on a dataset
rows.operation_detail: Measured layer firing rates with diffusion-rate weight selection, with and without firing-rate-collapse correction.
rows.value: With correction, firing rate remains around target rate quite reliably; optimal weights found were 0.0387
rows.uncertainty: Standard error in the mean for 5 trials
rows.locator: Figure 8 left and accompanying text, section 5
rows.note: Input spikes were Poisson trains at the target rate; parameters τ = 10ms, I = 0.6, Vr = 0, Vth = 1.
rows.check: Maintaining firing rates at initialization does not establish faster learning or greater trainable depth. The selected weight 0.0387 is a setup parameter, not an outcome.

rows.subject: Feed-forward SNN with 20 layers
rows.stage_stated: initialization simulation; not trained on a dataset
rows.operation_detail: Measured layer firing rates with diffusion-rate weight selection, with and without firing-rate-collapse correction.
rows.value: At high enough rates, firing rate with correction does not go to zero but converges to some value; optimal weights found were 0.0299
rows.uncertainty: Standard error in the mean for 5 trials
rows.locator: Figure 8 right and accompanying text, section 5
rows.note: The text also says lower target rates bias toward a slightly higher rate; the 10Hz result is in Supplementary Figure S3.
rows.check: The value misattributes the high-rate nonzero convergence observation: the text associates it with firing-rate collapse in Figure 8 left, the 50Hz setting, rather than the corrected 20Hz setting. Record the corrected 20Hz firing-rate trace separately. The selected weight 0.0299 is a setup parameter. Neither measures a claim version.

rows.subject: Feed-forward SNN with 20 layers
rows.stage_stated: initialization simulation; not trained on a dataset
rows.operation_detail: Compared variance of spike gradients across layers with and without surrogate-gradient scaling κ.
rows.measure: Variance of spike gradient ∆si across layers
rows.value: κ-corrected gradient remains nearly constant; variance still decays to some extent
rows.note: The paper states that a larger Bth = 0.1 gives much worse variance propagation because Assumption 13 fails; Supplementary Figure S4.
rows.check: Surrogate-gradient variance at initialization does not establish learning speed or trainable depth. The intervention scales the surrogate derivative rather than comparing weight initializations during training.
